## Details

### elekloader

Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. 2026-11-12 (main): core-a4mk2 0.6 brings core-ar2 0.10-0.13's foundations to the Analog Four MKII (field defaults, the modified mark, the project-save event, payloads, knob looks, screen calls) and a 37.7 MB mods' area. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them. 2026-11-13 (main): a third file family, ELE2, for the Analog Rytm MKI OS 1.74 (Modwerk's Rytm MKI research holds the measurements behind the profile); the README's table also names 1.73, the profile only 1.74. core-ot 0.9-0.40 opens about 40 more Octatrack events and tables to mods (mutes, sequencer moments, LFO waves, popup rows, PATTERN SETTINGS and PERSONALIZE rows, the playback increment, card file calls, the engine task's jobs, a block to DSP core 1).

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument.org and the repo (read 2026-10-31): canonical repo is github.com/elekloader/elekloader (183 commits, 103 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later); web app moved to elekloader.github.io/elekloader; the Mac app was absent from v0.9.0 because signing secrets need renewing. v0.9.0 cores: core-4.1 and core-4.1-os1.54 (Digitakt mk1), core-dn1-4.1.1 and -os1.44 (Digitone mk1), core-ar2-0.8 (Analog Rytm MKII 1.74), core-ot-0.8 (Octatrack 1.40C), core-mc-0.3 (Model:Cycles), core-ms-0.1 (Model:Samples), core-a4 0.1-0.4 (Analog Four MKII 1.56). Kit 0.7.0 catalog: 19 cores, 88 mods. machine-pages 1.2/1.3/1.5 need core 3.0+ on Digitakt mk1 and refuse NEIGHBOR 0.6, SOPHIE 1.1.13 and digichain-based machine mods beside them; fxkit 0.1 gives Digitone effect mods a shared mixer, two LFOs, pattern p-locks and a CPU guard; core-dn1 4.1 adds ev_note_queue; kit 0.6.0 gives 4.0 cores larger RAM areas (256 KB Digitakt, 1.25 MB Digitone). docs/ includes AGENTS.md, DEVICES.md, MACHINES-DN2, SHARC-DN2, CORES, FORMAT, BUILDING, ADAPTING (not all read yet - see hardware/MINING.md). The earlier irpina/elekloader repo is where the author's older releases lived._

_Related: uses tool `digikit` (README: checks or gates run in digikit's emulator (not shipped)) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: forum thread 30, GitHub release v0.4.0, gearnews, dubspot, DEVICES.md, ADAPTING.md, seqrows-ot README (2026-11-13)_

### Modwerk (formerly Octamod)

2026-11-12: the Octatrack card firmware builder is retired: modules reach an Octatrack only through the Modwerk base, over USB or as one set file (MODWERK0.SET) on the card; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save paused until they have base versions; Spectrum, Modulation, Character and MIDI Scenes removed for good; CPU-rendered machines get a budget (CPU FULL) after FM Synth froze an MKII (I79); POLY8 and FM Synth carry a Heavy CPU badge; checks refuse writes into the stock DELAY table and odd jump targets; the DT2 base hides the raw +Drive block write from modules; Octatrack modules moved to sdk/octatrack/modules; new experimental Crossfader and Live Looper for the Digitakt I (OS 1.54) and Amiga, a tracker-style sample machine, for the Octatrack. 2026-11-11/12: the Octatrack base and USB installs are open to everyone (first install still from the card, at most 20 modules per set; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save card-only); USB Audio is off unless the set has the USB Audio module; skipping modules at boot moved from FUNC to holding PROJ at power-on (MKI keeps FUNC); the octabam pin is frozen (Modwerk follows only elekloader upstream); Analog BD 0.1.7 has a new 909 model; base-update and SYNTIZ incidents I75 and I76. 2026-11-09/10: Octatrack beta: the silence after USB DISK MODE (finding 72) was the base mistaking stock's DSP pause for a stall, fixed (I69); FM Synth with many FLEX tracks no longer loses the audio on PLAY; the Octatrack page asks for a power cycle when the DSP has stopped; Temp Save 0.1.0 withdrawn from USB installs (card build stays). Modwerk also loads effects onto Zoom MultiStomp pedals now (ZDL files over USB; not an Elektron device). Browser-based hub, builds locally from the user's own stock OS. Browse mods by device, forum with a section per device, shared SDK. Dubspot (13 Oct): several modules are still early prototypes. last_activity = date of the Dubspot article, not a forum post. 2026-11-02: three Analog Rytm MKII modules by npp1993 moved into the library (Pipo Loop 0.1.1, Sample RATE 0.1.0, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.6.0, all experimental, OS 1.74; linkable together with core-ar2 0.7, Filter Hz and Loop Sync; the packages themselves not yet run on a unit). `_submissions/` takes no new modules. The Octatrack USB beta also works on the MKI. 2026-11-03: the site now lets you download a built Analog Rytm MKII .syx (after confirming you know how to get back to stock); new Rytm module quick-velocity-aftertouch-assign with a verification note. Zoom pedals: an effect whose group+ID clashes with one already on the pedal is moved to a free local Delay ID 958-1023 (ID only in the ZDL header at 0x40-0x41, no checksum); two effects with the same group and ID froze an MS-70CDR at boot until its ROM was reprogrammed. 2026-11-04/05: Rytm MKII downloads on (records); npp1993's Control In Actions (footswitch or 0-5 V gate on EXP/CV IN as ACTION for MUTE and more) and Quick Velocity+Aftertouch Assign join the library, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.7.0; euclidean 1.1.6 for Digitakt I 1.53/1.54 reported working on a unit by sumedho (all cases, save/reload, power cycle). 2026-11-08 to 11-10 (74c9eb2): Rytm library gains comp-preview, kit-ab, lfo-rnd and voice-dac (from rytm2_mods, unit runs on the Modwerk base), ctrl-in-perf and scene-mutes (from rytm-mods-src 0017/0018, unit runs T208/T210/T221), Improved Machine Browser and MIDI Mute; the Octatrack key bus moved to the tail of the first FX2 slot (checked on an MKI and an MKII); a Digitakt II audio scheduler is proposed (emulator only); Zoom MS-70CDR pedal work (out of scope here). 2026-11-12/13: Octatrack base: a stall record now keeps the 128 frames before it; an installed Sidechain no longer causes NO ROOM on every pick after a restart (I96); a new USB device revision (bcdDevice 0x0101) repairs Windows hosts that could not open the unit (I100); a machine engine's DSP price moved into its package; the base refuses a module machine or effect pick while the CPU meter is at 85 % or more; VECTOR 0.3.2 fixes a whole-bank reset (I95); SYNTIZ and Tape Echo get a Heavy CPU badge. Rytm MKII: the send-bus base gains digital voices; new Improved AMP and BD ANALOG (I97-I99). module:doctor covers Digitakt II modules; a Digitakt II pre-send render hook is proposed (emulator only). FRACT, an Octatrack granular machine draft by ex1010, has a functional unit report (2026-11-10).

_Related: cites `elekloader` (README mentions elekloader (porting from it / hosted loader)); cites `octabam` (README: porting from octabam is part of the module guide) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### Chopshop

Browser builder for Rytm MK1/MKII OS 1.73 (CHOP with step locks, sample focus, per-track cuts) and Analog Keys OS 1.56 (chord memory, joystick random). Not OS 1.74, not Analog Four. Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later; distribution: browser-installer. Listed by altstrument.

### libanalogrytm

C library that decodes and encodes Rytm SysEx (kits, sounds, patterns, settings, projects); no MIDI I/O. Dormant since 2023. Licence: MIT; distribution: source-only. Listed by altstrument; repo not read by us yet.

### rytm-builder

Assembles Rytm project SysEx from a library of pattern/kit dumps (Rust CLI and a Mac app); does not send MIDI. OS 1.70 object layout. Licence: MIT; distribution: source-only. Listed by altstrument; repo not read by us yet.

### rytm-mods-src

Public copy of MrScruff's Rytm MKII OS 1.73 mods (euclid accents, velocity humanise, random LFO, kit A/B, slice loop, control-all and more). Licence: GPL-2.0-only; distribution: patch-your-own. Listed by altstrument. Also reachable as connorway32/rytm-mods-src (same HEAD 3a98e23, 2026-11-03). 2026-11-08: 0017 lets a CTRL IN jack in CV or EXPR mode drive one of the performance macros PF1-PF12 (device-wide setting); 0018 lets a scene store track mutes (SCENE held, FUNC + trig), kept per kit in the project. Its re/subsystems notes (control inputs, scenes and mutes, the "loosened" kit and sound bytes) are folded into hardware/devices/analog-rytm.md.

_Related: uses tool `elektron-firmware-tool` (README: fetched and built into vendor/ by setup, not shipped); mod for `modwerk` (modwerk sdk/analog-rytm-mkii/modules ctrl-in-perf and scene-mutes name mods/0017-ctrl-in-perf and mods/0018-scene-mutes of this repo as source) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-01), README (2026-11-11)_

### Sidecar | Expander

A Raspberry Pi 4B/5 on the Rytm's USB port adds digital voices, effects and a sequencer; the Rytm runs a patched OS. 0.3.2 adds experimental, emulator-only Digitakt support. The Teensy variant is frozen. GPL-2.0. On 2026-11-09, Analog Four MKII support since 0.4.0 (A4 firmware a4-v0.12, OS 1.56); 0.4.3 caps the Rytm screen redraws after users saw a sluggish Rytm at 20-40 redraws a second. 2026-11-13: a card config editor on the documentation site writes the Pi's config.txt and cmdline.txt in the browser.

_Related: mod for `elekloader` (README: the Rytm firmware part is an elekloader module); uses tool `analog-emu` (README: built or checked in trigcondition/analog-emu) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### Analog Rytm MK1 OS 1.74 mods

Sister project of the A4 MK1 mods (same registry/verify method). Adds Machinedrum TX-8/TX-9 ports as new machines, a chorus as a third send, a sidechain-style duck at the voices' analog VCAs, and a CPU-load probe build. Has hazards and flashing docs. MIT.

### rytm-mods boot report

Evidence for Modwerk's add-a-machine steps on the Rytm MKII - the stock file rebuilt byte for byte, a modified OS booted on a unit and recovered with stock, and elekloader's core-ar2 with every shared event observed on a unit. Hashes, addresses and photos only. GPL-2.0.

_Related: uses tool `elekloader` (README: elekloader's core-ar2 with two test mods run on a unit); cites `modwerk` (README: written for Modwerk's Add a machine steps) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### TurboMIDI (C++)

Header-only C++ implementation of Elektron's TurboMIDI speed negotiation (up to 20x DIN MIDI speed). Since 2026-11-04 the repo no longer answers anonymously (git asks for credentials, so private or removed); still gone on 2026-11-11, so it is no longer polled.

Rust abstractions over the Rytm's undocumented SysEx (bindings to a fork of bsp2's libanalogrytm). MIT.

### Plock (Rytm pattern editor)

Browser pattern editor for the Analog Rytm over Web MIDI: pulls the current pattern and kit by SysEx, edits trigs, parameter locks, retrigs, micro-timing and sound locks in a step grid and sends the result back; opens and saves .syx dumps and exports MIDI. The README credits earlier community work on the format. MIT per README (no licence file in the repo).

_Related: cites `libanalogrytm` (README credits: byte layouts derived from libanalogrytm) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-03), README_

### ElekPrep (elektron-sample-prep)

Single-page browser sample prep: trims at zero crossings, converts to 48 kHz 16-bit WAV, works out loop lengths from BPM and steps; profiles for four devices (device list taken from the related ElekPrep Transfer app, not checked). No MIDI; files go to the unit through Transfer or Elektroid. MIT.

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-03), README_

### ElekPrep Transfer

Closed-source browser app that preps audio and sends it over Web MIDI SysEx to the +Drive, with Transfer and +Drive Manager views and device profiles for Digitakt II, Digitakt, Analog Rytm (MKI/MKII) and Model:Samples. Proprietary; author not named. Relation to luizvarela's ElekPrep not established (same name). Interesting as a second independent implementation of +Drive upload over SysEx.

_Sources: altstrument (2026-11-03)_

### Elektron Project Companion

Windows editor for arranging live sets from local project backups: place patterns in banks A-H and export a new project for Transfer. Rytm MKII: .arprj and whole-project .syx (patterns, kits, sound locks, sample references). Digitakt II: .dt2prj project image v4 (patterns with their kits; merging only with identical sample pools, since relocating a sample changes locks). File-level testing on a real OS. Licence not stated. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07.

_Sources: GitHub search 2026-11-07, README_

### Sidecar | Expander: Rytm mods

The source of the Analog Rytm MKII OS mods that Sidecar | Expander needs: patch sources, symbol map, allocation registry and the build that turns the user's own stock .syx into a modded one, as one elekloader module per OS; the Analog Four MKII's mod in a4/. 0.4.0 reports each track's pan and route (stereo through mode), adds MD's own page, preset browsers for JUNO and 6-OP FM, DSP SAMPLE's sample picker, list knobs of up to 36 names, a MIDI machine (machine 50) and arpeggiator settings in the sound. Sidecar Mini (Teensy) is frozen at 0.1.0.

_Related: same project `sidecar-expander` (README: the Rytm mods that Sidecar | Expander uses); mod for `elekloader` (README: one elekloader module per OS) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-10, README, README (2026-11-11)_

### elkbench (hardware tests as an MCP server)

One local MCP server per PC that gives AI agent sessions the same tools for testing Elektron units (Analog Rytm MKII, Analog Four MKII, Digitone; Digitakt untested on hardware) and their emulators: claim a unit, run a test plan, flash an OS, take screenshots, record and check USB audio, take or restore an Overbridge Total Recall image. It enforces one owner per unit, emulator first, and a hardware run only after the person says go. Python stdlib; Windows and Linux. 2026-11-10: a flash between two fixed OS files of a unit can reuse an emulator pass of the same flash, recorded with the hashes of the emulator, the flash tool and the card, while all of them stay the same. 2026-11-11 (config example): an optional emulator headroom check waits for CPU, free RAM and a cap on running emulators before each emulator start. 2026-11-12: emulator timing (analog-emu unit or exact timing, the Sidecar's Overbridge stream on the Rytm) and a CPU gate that fails an emulator run at 95 % CPU. 2026-11-13: elklock marks a unit that stalled on its restart after a flash and refuses every device command on it until a watched power cycle (elkflash usb-cycle).

_Related: uses tool `analog-emu` (README: emulator first; sidecar-emu reaches analog-emu through it) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-10, README_

### sidecar-emu (Sidecar emulator)

QEMU cut down to the Raspberry Pi 4B and the devices Sidecar's engine needs: boots the Sidecar engine image, answers over Ethernet, puts an Analog Rytm MKII stand-in on its USB-A side and gives its USB-C gadget a raw MIDI TCP port, so an OS upgrade or an elkbench run can go through the emulated Pi into analog-emu. A local experiment, not meant for QEMU upstream.

_Related: uses tool `analog-emu` (README: through the emulated Pi into analog-emu); cites `sidecar-expander` (README: emulates the Sidecar engine) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: state/NEW.md 2026-11-10, README_
